title: Capacity Futures & Operator Runway Roadmap
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This roadmap defines our multi-quarter strategy for 'capacity futures' — the set of tooling, dashboards, alerting, and operator workflows that keep Redwood's inference platform within SLOs while preserving economic predictability. It focuses on three outcomes: predictable regional capacity, clear operator runway during surges, and automated candidate mitigations that reduce human toil.

Background and motivation
-------------------------
- Problem: Demand for hosted and dedicated inference is increasingly bursty and correlated across tenants (batch jobs, nightly retrains, marketing spikes). Past incidents showed operators were reactive: capacity decisions were manual, noisy, and slow.
- Goal: Give operators the right predictive signals + prescriptive actions so we can avoid emergency model swaps and expensive spot replenishment.

Scope and principles
--------------------
- Scope: Roadmap covers forecasting pipelines, operator dashboards, alert rule library, a prescriptive escalation ladder (human + automated), and a compact operator training curriculum.
- Principles:
  - Signal-first: dashboards must show leading signals (queue growth, prefix-cache miss slope), not just lagging token errors.
  - Prescriptive actions: every alert should point to a 1–3 step remediation playbook.
  - Economies-aware: decisions should include token-cost delta and SLA impact.
  - Small blast radius: test automations in canary region before global rollout.

Quarterly roadmap (high level)
------------------------------
- Q4 2026: Forecasting baseline + operator runway UI
  - Deliver a 30/90-day capacity forecast pipeline (rwd-forecast) with tenant-level confidence bands.
  - Launch Operator Runway UI (Grafana + React) showing projected SLO burn and recommended mitigations.
- Q1 2027: Automated pre-emptive mitigations + alert library
  - Integrate forecast outputs with traffic-steering service for soft re-routing.
  - Publish standard alert rule set and templates for token-surge, KV-cache collapse, and prefetch starvation.
- Q2 2027: Cost-aware autoscaler and safe-rollback DSL
  - Autoscaler gains cost-aware policy knobs (max-token-cost-per-minute, tenant-priority-weight).
  - Introduce a rollback DSL for automated mitigation undo when secondary signals degrade.
- Q3 2027: Operator training, canary, and retrospective cadence
  - Run operator gamedays against synthetic surges, finalize runbook library, and lock SLO contracts for major mitigations.

Metrics and acceptance criteria
-------------------------------
Table: primary metrics and target thresholds (acceptance criteria)

Metric | Baseline (2026-10) | Target (end Q2 2027)
------|--------------------:|---------------------:
P99 tail token latency (hosted) | 850ms | <=700ms
Operator mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for token-surge | 42m | <15m
Incidents requiring emergency model swap per quarter | 3 | <=1
Forecast precision (30d, MAPD) | 28% | <=12%
Operator toil hours saved (per month) | NA | >=80h

Ownership, roles and stakeholders
----------------------------------
- Product owner: Priya Raman (Platform Product)
- Technical lead: Diego Alvarez (Platform Systems)
- Operator champion: Lina Torres (Platform Ops)
- Data science: forecasting models maintained by Applied ML team (owner: Sameer Joshi)
- Customer success liaison: Aria Patel (to coordinate dedicated customer constraints)

Implementation plan (detailed)
-----------------------------
1) Forecast pipeline (rwd-forecast) — Q4 2026
   - Inputs: historical per-tenant qps, sequence-length distribution, eviction rates, scheduled promotions (marketing calendar).
   - Output: daily artifact (30/90/365 day) with mean and 95% CI by tenant/region.
   - Health checks: data drift alerts when MAPD > 20% for 3 consecutive runs.

2) Operator Runway UI — Q4 2026
   - Panels: projected SLO burn, forecasted capacity gap, recommended mitigations (soft reroute, burst pool increase, prefetch boost).
   - Interaction: single-click to create mitigation ticket (Jira) or trigger a safe test (canary).

3) Alert library and prescriptive playbooks — Q1 2027
   - Rules grouped by domain: latency-signals, capacity-signals, cache-signals, cost-telemetry.
   - Each rule includes: severity, SRE owner, step-by-step playbook, quick links to dashboards and CLI.

4) Cost-aware autoscaler and rollback DSL — Q2 2027
   - New autoscaler policy fields (example YAML):

   autoscale_policy: |
     min_replicas: 2
     max_replicas: 50
     cost_budget_per_minute_usd: 12.50
     priority_weights:
       tenant_default: 1.0
       tenant_critical: 3.0
     rollback_conditions:
       - metric: p95_latency
         direction: up
         threshold_ms: 900
         hold_for: 300s

5) Operator gamedays & retro loop — Q3 2027
   - Monthly synthetic exercise (in sandbox region) for the first 3 months post-rollout.
   - Post-gameday retro to capture runbook gaps and SLI blindspots.

Runbook excerpts (for common scenarios)
---------------------------------------
Scenario A: Rapid token-surge detected (queue growth > 25% in 120s)
1. Pager: Severity P1 to oncall operator.
2. Quick checks (3 mins):
   - rwdctl inspect queue --tenant $TENANT --region $REGION
   - check prefix-cache miss rate: rwdctl metrics query "prefix_cache_miss_rate{tenant=\"$TENANT\"}" --window 5m
3. Prescribed mitigations (in order):
   a) Soft reroute to warm secondary region (if latency budget allows).
      - CLI: rwdctl traffic steer --from $REGION --to $REGION2 --strategy gradual --duration 15m
   b) Trigger priority-shed: reduce low-priority tenant weight by 30%.
      - CLI: rwdctl tenant adjust-weight --tenant low-priority-queue --multiplier 0.7
   c) If still failing, spin controlled burst-capacity: rwdctl capacity burst-request --pool dedicated-burst --count 4
4. Post-mitigation: annotate incident ticket with chosen mitigations and monitoring links.

Scenario B: KV-prefix-cache collapse (sustained miss rate > 40% for 10m)
1. Immediate action: enable read-through cache fallback on affected model-variant.
   - API snippet: POST /api/v1/models/{m}/fallback-policy {"fallback": "read-through", "ttl_sec": 300}
2. If read-through causes backend saturation, throttle retrains and inform Applied ML.
3. Run cache warmup job for top-200 hot prefixes: rwdctl cache warmup --prefix-file hot-prefixes.csv

Dashboards and alert templates
------------------------------
Example alert (YAML) for token-surge:

alert: TokenSurgeForecastBreach
expr: forecast_gap_percentage_by_tenant > 20
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: critical
  owner: platform-systems
annotations:
  summary: "Forecast gap > 20% for tenant {{ $labels.tenant }} in {{ $labels.region }}"
  runbook: "https://confluence/internal/eng-platform/runbooks/token-surge-mitigation"

Alert thresholds table (operator-facing)

Condition | Severity | Immediate action
---------|---------|------------------
forecast_gap > 20% | P2 | Notify operator, prepare soft reroute
queue_growth > 25% in 120s | P1 | Pager + immediate mitigations (see runbook)
prefix_cache_miss_rate > 40% for 10m | P1 | Fallback + cache warmup job
cost_budget_exhausted_in_5m | P2 | Evaluate priority shed or temporary cap on burst pool

Testing and canary plan
------------------------
- Canary target: single non-critical region with 5% of production traffic.
- Canary tests:
  - Synthetic workload spike (1.5x baseline for 20m)
  - Forecast perturbation injection: add synthetic scheduled promotion event to pipeline
- Success criteria for canary: no P1 incidents, forecast MAPD <= 15%, operator MTTM <= 20m.

Risks and mitigations
---------------------
- Risk: False positives from forecast cause unnecessary scaling (cost).
  - Mitigation: keep a human-in-the-loop for high-cost actions and apply cooldown windows.
- Risk: Autoscaler oscillations after cost-aware policies introduced.
  - Mitigation: conservative defaults, ramp-up windows, and rollback DSL enforcement.
- Risk: Operator cognitive load increases with new signals.
  - Mitigation: invest in UI affordances, one-click remediations, and monthly belt-training.

Operator training curriculum (compact)
-------------------------------------
- Module 1: Read the forecast — understanding confidence bands and MAPD.
- Module 2: Runbook drills — token surge, cache collapse, spot depletion.
- Module 3: Safe automations — when to approve autoscaler actions.
- Module 4: Post-incident blameless retros — capturing metrics, decisions, and follow-ups.

Retro cadence and continuous improvement
---------------------------------------
- Weekly: Quick incident review (if any) with annotated mitigations linked.
- Monthly: Forecast accuracy review and parameter tuning session (forecast team + platform).
- Quarterly: Full gameday + executive summary (product + eng leadership).

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets and queries
----------------------------------------
- Check tenant forecast: rwdctl forecast get --tenant $TENANT --window 30d --output table
- Estimate cost delta for mitigation: rwdctl cost simulate --mitigation "burst+reroute" --duration 30m --tenant $TENANT
- Generate hot-prefix list: rwdctl metrics query "top_prefixes{region=\"us-west-2\"}" --limit 200 > hot-prefixes.csv
